items.q: Florence Cadrez, who is still around and a very lovely, wonderful woman

ctx.x: of this, you know, he explained all of this to you, and he would take the time and go on to explain to you the advantages of being in the union. He says, 'Now, when you work you have a chance of making more money.' And he says, 'Not only that, if you don't get your money the union can protect you. The union is a protective association and they will see that you get your money.' So all this sounded very good to me. It did sound (Inaudible). And he just took the time to explain all of the advantages of being a…
Well, Paul Howard was the Secretary. Florence Cadrez, who is still around and a very lovely, wonderful woman, and she was the corresponding secretary.

Paul was the financial secretary. I'm trying to think who was the Treasurer. Well, I guess Paul was both, Paul Howard, because he really, he just took good care of that money and those books like you would never believe, you know. He was both. And then later on Ed Bailey I think was the President, and he served for awhile, you know, while I was in the union. And, well, that was it.
